pull.title: KAFKA-21368: Lift non-public config key strings into public
pull.body:
`o.a.k.clients.CommonClientConfigs` is not part of the public interface
to Apache Kafka. It is neither in the javadoc nor is it marked
`@InterfaceAudience.Public`. However, a handful of the config keys for
producer, consumer, and streams were defined in this class, essentially
meaning that an application using the string constants was stepping
outside the Kafka public interface.

For example, `CommonClientConfigs.METADATA_RECOVERY_STRATEGY_CONFIG`
which is allowed as a producer config should really be
`ProducerConfig.METADATA_RECOVERY_STRATEGY_CONFIG`. The latter is in a
properly public class.

This PR adds all of the missing string constants to `ProducerConfig`,
`ConsumerConfig` and `StreamsConfig`.

It is debatable whether this is tidying up the code by implementing the
intent of KIPs, or whether it needs a KIP. For example, KIP-1242 added
`metadata.cluster.check.enable` as a config for producer, consumer and
admin. In explicably, the constant was added to `CommonClientConfigs`
(not public) and `AdminClientConfigs`, but not `ProducerConfig` nor
`ConsumerConfig`. This was a simple omission and was the intent of the
KIP (which I wrote).

Reviewers: Chia-Ping Tsai <chia7712@gmail.com>

repo.name: kafka
repo.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

reviews.body: @AndrewJSchofield thanks for this patch. I think those public APIs have been missing for a long while. It is truly an issue after `CommonClientConfigs` was marked as non-public API.

review_comments.body: Should we follow the naming convention by adding the `_CONFIG` suffix?
Should we update this `CommonClientConfigs#BOOTSTRAP_RESOLVE_TIMEOUT_MS_CONFIG` as well?

There could perhaps be `o.a.k.common.serialization.SerializerConfigs` or similar because the public classes in that package do still refer to `CommonClientConfigs` and don't have any legitimate alternative as far as I can see.
